title: Secondary Science: Explore the Water Cycle
subject: science
disclaimer: This is a conceptual activity model, not a weather forecast or a quantitative weather prediction. Solar energy, atmospheric cooling and droplet growth are simplified teaching controls. Real weather also depends on humidity, winds, pressure and cloud microphysics.

beats.label: Whole cycle
beats.narration: Follow one parcel of water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection. The same water circulates; it does not disappear.

beats.label: Evaporation
beats.narration: Solar energy helps liquid water change into water vapour. Water vapour is an invisible gas, not a cloud of visible droplets.

beats.label: Condensation
beats.narration: Moist air cools and water vapour condenses into tiny liquid droplets. Cooling alone cannot create water where no water vapour is present.

beats.label: Precipitation
beats.narration: Cloud droplets can grow through collisions and other processes. When drops become large enough to fall, we see precipitation. A cloud does not always mean rain.

beats.label: Collection
beats.narration: Rainwater collects in rivers, lakes and the sea; some enters the soil or flows as runoff. Evaporation can start the journey again.

check.question: If moist air cools but cloud droplets do not grow enough, does rain necessarily follow?
options: Yes. Every cloud must produce rain.
No. Cooling can cause condensation without precipitation.
Yes. Cooling turns water vapour directly into rain.
check.explanation: Condensation forms small cloud droplets. Precipitation requires additional growth and suitable conditions; not all clouds produce rain.
